cases.situation: I'm Sam, going to a fintech conference alone next week, mainly for the fraud panel. I freeze up at the coffee breaks. Give me something to say to someone standing by the coffee.
cases.reply: Hi, I'm Sam. Which session brought you here? I'm mostly here for the fraud panel.
cases.note: One question plus one line about you. The next question comes from their answer: 'What's the part people don't get about that?'

cases.situation: 每周一在电梯里都会碰到隔壁部门的李姐，我只知道她上个月去新疆玩了。每次都尴尬地各自看手机。
cases.reply: 李姐早！上个月去新疆，哪一站最值得去？
cases.note: 记得对方说过的事最管用；接下来的问题从她的回答里找，别换话题。

cases.situation: At my girlfriend Amy's work party, chatting with a guy named Chris who's given me one-word answers twice now. Amy's the only person I know here and we're standing right by the food table. I want to give it one more go before I move on.
cases.reply: I'll be honest, Amy's the only person I know here, so I've mostly been guarding the food table. Anything on it worth the trip?
cases.note: Two flat answers is the cue to share one thing about yourself to lower the pressure. If it stays flat, say it was good to meet him and move on without making it a verdict on either of you.

cases.situation: At my friend Lena's birthday drinks, a guy called Owen just told me he's a sign language interpreter, mostly in hospitals. I've never met an interpreter, my mind went blank and I just said 'oh, cool'. I want a follow-up that isn't 'that must be interesting'.
cases.reply: Hang on, I said 'cool' and moved on too fast. I've never met an interpreter before. What's the part of the job people usually don't get?
cases.note: The second question comes from his first answer: ask for the view only he has, follow whatever he picks, and share one small thing back before the next question.

cases.situation: First video call with my new team and I'm always early. It'll probably be just me and Inês, who's based in Lisbon, waiting for a few minutes. All I know is she's the data analyst.
cases.reply: Hi Inês, looks like we're the early ones. I'm the new one here, so I'll just ask: what's one thing about this team you wish someone had told you in your first month?
cases.note: Asks for a view she actually has, which gives a thread to follow; the next question should come from her answer.

cases.situation: 国庆回老家吃团圆饭，我旁边坐的是表姐的新老公，第一次见，只听表姐说过他在深圳做无人机。我怕冷场。
cases.reply: 姐夫，听我姐说你在深圳做无人机？我一直挺好奇的，你们做的是航拍那种，还是送快递、给庄稼打药那种？
cases.note: 问他有自己看法的事，然后顺着他的回答追问“当初怎么入的这行”；分享一句自己的，再把话头还给他。

cases.situation: At my neighbours Mark and Deb's barbecue I just asked a woman I met ten minutes ago, Grace, when her baby is due. She said 'I'm not pregnant' with a tight smile and now we're both standing by the grill in silence. What do I say right now?
cases.reply: That came out wrong, and I'm sorry, I shouldn't have assumed. So how do you know Mark and Deb?
cases.note: Fix it in one line and hand her a new thread straight away. A second apology makes the moment bigger than it was.

cases.situation: Tomorrow I'm driving two hours with my new boss, Graham, to a client site in Leeds. I've been here three weeks and barely know him, except that he mentioned in my first week he's training for the York marathon. How do I start?
cases.reply: So how's the training for York going? You mentioned it in my first week and I've been wondering how far the long runs are up to now.
cases.note: Open with the one thing you remember, follow his answer ('What got you into running?'), share one small thing back, and on a long drive let a quiet stretch be quiet.

cases.situation: On vient d'emménager à Lyon et je récupère ma fille à l'école tous les jours. Les autres parents se connaissent tous. Il y a un papa qui attend toujours au portail avec un grand chien roux, et ma fille ne parle que de ce chien.
cases.reply: Bonjour ! Ma fille ne parle que de votre chien depuis la rentrée. Il s'appelle comment ?
cases.note: Partir de ce qu'il y a sous les yeux, puis rebondir sur sa réponse et glisser une phrase sur vous (« On vient d'emménager ») avant de lui rendre la parole.

cases.situation: En la boda de mi prima en Sevilla me han sentado al lado del abuelo del novio, don Manuel, de 85 años. Solo sé que fue pescador en Cádiz toda la vida. No quiero pasar la cena en silencio.
cases.reply: Don Manuel, me han contado que fue usted pescador en Cádiz toda la vida. ¿Qué es lo que más echa de menos del mar?
cases.note: Pregunta por algo sobre lo que él tiene opinión, y saca la siguiente pregunta de su respuesta, no de una lista.

cases.situation: Matched with Sam on Hinge. We've done 'how was your weekend' / 'good, you?' twice and it's dying. Their profile says they just got back from climbing in Kalymnos and are learning Greek 'badly'. I once did a month of Greek on an app and can mostly say 'the cat drinks milk'.
cases.reply: Okay, I have to ask about Kalymnos. Was it the climbing that got you there, or did the Greek come first? I did a month of Greek on an app once and can mostly say 'the cat drinks milk'.
cases.note: Swap generic questions for something they chose to show you, share one small thing back, and end on a question they'll enjoy answering.

cases.situation: At my friend Nadia's housewarming on Saturday, someone will definitely ask 'so what do you do?' I was laid off in August after six years at Halden Bank, and I've been using the time to learn to bake bread. I don't want to lie or kill the conversation.
cases.reply: Right now I'm between jobs. I was at Halden Bank for six years until August, and the upside is I've finally had time to learn to bake bread. How do you know Nadia?
cases.note: One honest sentence, one small thing you'd happily talk about, then hand the thread back to them.

cases.situation: 大学毕业十年的同学聚会上，一个男生特别热情地走过来叫出我的名字，还说记得我当年在辩论队。我完全想不起他叫什么，也不记得当年熟不熟。
cases.reply: 你记性也太好了，连辩论队都记得！我得先坦白，十年没见，你的名字我一下卡住了，真不好意思，提醒我一下？你当年也常来看我们比赛吗？
cases.note: 忘了名字就一句话坦白，别硬撑着聊；马上接住他给的话头，尴尬几秒就过去了。

cases.situation: I'm picking up a client, Ji-woo Park, from her hotel tomorrow morning for the 20-minute drive to our Chicago office. She flew in from Seoul last night and it's her first time in the US. I don't want to talk shop the whole way or sit in silence.
cases.reply: Welcome to Chicago, Ji-woo. How are you holding up after the flight? If you get a free evening while you're here, is there anything you're hoping to see or eat?
cases.note: A visitor has a view on her own trip: follow her answer, offer one local tip of your own, then hand it back.

cases.situation: I'm Rob, at the reception after my coworker Dana's dad's funeral. I never met him. I'm standing by the tea urn next to an older man I don't know and the silence is getting awkward.
cases.reply: Hi, I'm Rob, I work with Dana. I never got to meet her dad. How did you know him?
cases.note: At a funeral, invite a story rather than an opinion. If he shares one, 'What was he like?' keeps it going, and quiet moments can stay quiet.

cases.situation: My sister's 15-year-old son Kai is staying with us this weekend and answers everything with 'fine' or a shrug. My sister told me he just started playing bass in a band with friends from school.
cases.reply: Your mum says you've started playing bass in a band. What are you lot playing at the moment, covers or your own stuff?
cases.note: Teenagers shut down at questions about school; ask about the thing they chose.

cases.situation: I'm Tom, a junior analyst on the analytics team, and I just ended up alone in the lift with our CEO, Margaret Osei, for about eight floors. The only thing I know is that at last week's all-hands she talked about the new Glasgow office opening in November.
cases.reply: Hi, I'm Tom from the analytics team. At the all-hands last week you mentioned the Glasgow office opening in November. How's it coming along?
cases.note: With someone senior, one specific question about their project beats flattery or a pitch; let them do the talking.

cases.situation: 美容師です。今日初めて来店されるお客様のカウンセリングシートに「趣味：キャンプ」「会話：少しなら」と書いてあった。カットは1時間くらい。話しかけすぎず、でも気まずくならない最初のひと言が知りたい。
cases.reply: キャンプがお好きなんですね。最近はどのあたりに行かれました？お疲れのときは、目を閉じてゆっくりしていただいて大丈夫ですからね。
cases.note: 「少しなら」は合図。質問はひとつだけにして、返事が短ければ静かな時間をそのまま任せる。

cases.situation: At my cousin Emma's wedding to Josh, the man next to me at the reception, Gary, has just started on about the mayor's new bike lanes and clearly wants me to agree. I don't want a debate at a wedding. The only other thing I know is he said he flew in from Denver this morning.
cases.reply: Ha, I think that one's a debate for another day, I'm keeping tonight strictly about cake. You flew in from Denver this morning, right? How do you know Emma and Josh?
cases.note: Politics needs a position; step around it with a smile rather than a counterpoint, then hand him a thread he can enjoy.

cases.situation: 楼下新搬来一家，上周末刚搬进来。男主人每天早上在小区里遛一只柯基，我住他们家楼上。今天在快递柜前又碰到他，一直只是点头，想说两句。
cases.reply: 你好，你们是上周末刚搬来的吧？我就住你们楼上。这只柯基我天天早上都能看到，太可爱了，它叫什么名字呀？
cases.note: 从狗问起，对方有得聊；接着顺着狗的名字或年龄往下问，再说一句自己的。

cases.situation: I'm Mia, doing an 8-week online UX course, and tonight we get put into Zoom breakout rooms of four for 10 minutes before the exercise starts. Last week everyone sat there with cameras on in total silence. All I know is the tutor said people are joining from London, Lagos and Toronto; I'm in London.
cases.reply: Hi all, I'm Mia, joining from London. Quick question to get us going: what time is it where you are, and what did you skip to be here?
cases.note: In a group call, one easy question everyone can answer breaks the silence; then follow the most interesting answer instead of going round the room again.

cases.situation: Ich gebe eine Einweihungsparty. Meine Kollegin Anke und mein Nachbar Jürgen stehen seit ein paar Minuten schweigend nebeneinander am Buffet. Anke ist gerade vom Wandern in Portugal zurück, und Jürgen will nächstes Jahr den Jakobsweg in Portugal gehen.
cases.reply: Anke, darf ich dir Jürgen vorstellen, meinen Nachbarn? Jürgen will nächstes Jahr den Jakobsweg in Portugal gehen, und Anke ist gerade vom Wandern dort zurück. Anke, wo genau warst du unterwegs?
cases.note: Als Gastgeber stellt man nicht nur vor, sondern legt beiden gleich den gemeinsamen Faden hin und eine erste Frage dazu.

cases.situation: I'm Claire, a partner at an architecture firm. At our intern welcome drinks tonight, one of the new interns, Ben, is standing alone near me looking nervous. All I know is he's from Glasgow and his portfolio had a library project with a reading room lit from the north.
cases.reply: Hi Ben, I'm Claire. I remember your library project from your portfolio, the reading room with the north light. What got you interested in libraries?
cases.note: When you're the senior one, ask about something they're proud of and let them talk; share one small thing back so it doesn't feel like an interview.

cases.situation: 坐高铁从北京去上海，要五个多小时。邻座是个三十岁左右的女生，在看迟子建的《额尔古纳河右岸》，这本我去年读过，特别喜欢。想聊两句，又怕打扰她看书。
cases.reply: 不好意思打扰一下，你在看《额尔古纳河右岸》呀？这本我去年读的，特别喜欢。你看到哪儿了？我保证不剧透，你想接着看书就当我没说哈。
cases.note: 在出不去的空间里搭话，开口就给对方一个轻松的台阶；她回得短，就让她安心看书。

cases.situation: 公司团建烧烤，我和财务部的小周聊了十几分钟，一直是我问她答，感觉像在面试她。她刚说最近周末在学手冲咖啡，老是冲得太酸。我自己每天早上就喝速溶。
cases.reply: 哈哈，那我得先坦白，我每天早上就是一包速溶打发的。冲得太酸是哪儿出了问题啊？
cases.note: 一直问会变成面试；先分享一句自己的，再顺着她刚说的往下问，别换新话题。

cases.situation: 健身房认识的刘哥，每次练完都在休息区聊几句。今天他突然问：“你们做程序员的，一个月得三四万吧？”我不想聊工资，但也不想冷场。他上周说在准备11月的半程马拉松。
cases.reply: 哈哈，这个可没那么夸张，我们这行也是各有各的难处。倒是你，11月的半马准备得怎么样了？现在一次能跑多少公里？
cases.note: 钱这类话题一句轻松带过，不解释也不反问；马上递一个他自己关心的话头，他再追问就笑着重复一句“没那么夸张”。

cases.situation: We're hosting a 16-year-old exchange student, Haruto, from Osaka for three weeks, and he arrives tonight. His English is basic, and his profile says he loves baseball and his mum's okonomiyaki. I know nothing about baseball, and I want an easy first thing to say at dinner that doesn't feel like a quiz.
cases.reply: Welcome, Haruto! You like baseball? Do you play, or watch? I know nothing about baseball, so you can teach me.
cases.note: With limited English, short sentences and an either-or question make answering easy; save the okonomiyaki for another night's thread.

cases.situation: I'm Leah, in the London finance team. Our company's Slack bot has paired me for a 'virtual coffee' with Tomás from the Madrid sales team, whom I've never met. His Slack status is a surfboard emoji and his profile says 'learning to surf, badly', I'm free most afternoons this week for the 20-minute call, and I want to send the first message so it doesn't feel like a form.
cases.reply: Hi Tomás, I'm Leah from finance in London, looks like the bot has matched us for coffee! I have to ask about the surfboard: where are you learning, and how badly are we talking? I'm free for 20 minutes any afternoon this week, whenever suits you.
cases.note: Open with the thing he chose to show, add one line about you, and let the next question come from his answer.

cases.situation: I've signed up with a befriending scheme, and tomorrow is my first Tuesday visit to Evelyn, 91, at her care home. The coordinator told me she was a primary school teacher for 40 years, and there's a framed photo of a little sailing boat on her windowsill. I'm Josh and I'm worried we'll just sit in silence.
cases.reply: Hello Evelyn, I'm Josh, I'll be coming to see you on Tuesdays. I couldn't help noticing the sailing boat on your windowsill. Is there a story behind it?
cases.note: Start from something in her room and let her stories lead; keep the teaching years for another visit, and let quiet stretches be quiet.

cases.situation: Entrei para o coral do bairro aqui em Porto Alegre há duas semanas e, no intervalo do ensaio, acabo ficando sozinha num canto. A senhora que canta ao meu lado, Dona Célia, está no coral há 20 anos e hoje trouxe um bolo de fubá para todo mundo. Quero puxar conversa com ela no intervalo de hoje.
cases.reply: Dona Célia, esse bolo de fubá está uma delícia, é receita de família? Eu entrei faz só duas semanas e ainda estou meio perdida por aqui. Vinte anos de coral, hein: como a senhora começou?
cases.note: Comece pelo que está na mesa e deixe a próxima pergunta sair da resposta dela.

cases.situation: Last month I asked my neighbour Frank to cut back his hedge because it was blocking our shared path. He did it within a week, but since then we just nod stiffly at each other. He's out most Saturday mornings polishing his old green convertible, and I'd like to break the ice this Saturday.
cases.reply: Morning, Frank! The path's been so much easier since you cut the hedge back, thank you. Is that convertible as much work as it looks, or is the Saturday polish the fun part?
cases.note: Thank him once for the hedge, then move straight to the thing he cares about; the thread to follow is the car, not the disagreement.

cases.situation: I'm Priya, at a local product managers' meetup where I don't know anyone. Three people by the drinks are debating whether AI note-takers in meetings are worth it, and I've just started trialling one at work. I want to join without barging in.
cases.reply: Mind if I join? I caught 'AI note-takers' and I've just started trialling one at work. I'm Priya. Are you finding they're worth it?
cases.note: Wait for a pause, give one line on why you're joining, then hand their own question back so you add to their thread instead of starting a new one. If they stay closed, 'enjoy the evening' and a smile is a fine exit.

cases.situation: I'm at a local tech meetup and have been chatting with Derek for 25 minutes about his home brewing; it was fun, and he's got me curious about trying a stout. I want to catch tonight's speaker, Amara, before she leaves, and I'd like to stay in touch with Derek.
cases.reply: Derek, this has been great, you've properly got me thinking about trying a stout. I want to catch Amara before she heads off, but I'd love to carry this on. Are you on LinkedIn?
cases.note: Exit on a high note with a real reason and a thread for next time, rather than waiting for the conversation to die.

cases.situation: For two months I've chatted with another mum at the poolside during our kids' Saturday swim lessons, and we've never swapped names; I only know her son is Arlo. Last week she said she was starting a pottery course on Wednesday evenings. I'm Hannah, and it feels too late to ask her name, but I want to.
cases.reply: I've just realised that after two months of Saturdays I don't know your name. I'm Hannah, by the way. So how was the first pottery class?
cases.note: Own the missing name lightly in one line so it's a shared joke, then pick up the thread she gave you last week.

cases.situation: 每周日晚上跟老家的爸爸视频，他总是“都挺好”“吃了”，三分钟就说挂了吧。妈妈偷偷告诉我，他今年在阳台种了一排辣椒，最近结果了，天天去看。我在上海，一盆植物都没养活过。
cases.reply: 爸，听妈说你阳台的辣椒结果了？结了多少个？把手机转过去让我看看呗。我在上海一盆植物都没养活过，你这手艺得教教我。
cases.note: 跟话少的长辈视频，问他正在用心的东西，最好让他拿给你看；接着顺着他的回答问“怎么种的”，别急着换话题。

cases.situation: I'm Jo. I met Zoe at a board game café night last Thursday and we swapped numbers; she texted 'great meeting you!', I replied 'you too!', and it's gone quiet. She'd mentioned she paints tiny figures for her games and was halfway through a dragon, and the most I've ever painted is my bedroom wall. I'd like to keep it going as friends, not as a date.
cases.reply: Hi Zoe, it's Jo from board game night. I've been wondering all week: did the dragon get finished? I'd love to see a photo. The most I've ever painted is my bedroom wall, so anything that small genuinely impresses me.
cases.note: Over text, pick up the thread she gave you and share one small thing back; if her reply is short, let it rest rather than sending more questions.

cases.situation: Mi compañera Lucía vuelve mañana a la oficina después de tres meses de baja. No sé por qué fue la baja y no quiero preguntar. Antes de irse siempre bajábamos juntas al café de las once y me contaba que estaba aprendiendo a tocar el ukelele; yo no sé tocar ningún instrumento.
cases.reply: ¡Lucía, qué bien tenerte de vuelta! Se te echaba de menos en el café de las once. Oye, ¿sigues con el ukelele? Yo sigo sin saber tocar ni la pandereta.
cases.note: Tras una baja no se pregunta el motivo: dale un tema suyo y, si ella saca lo demás, escucha sin insistir.

cases.situation: A plasterer, Marek, is redoing our living room walls all this week, and so far we've only said hello. He plays old jazz on a little radio all day, and I grew up with my grandad's jazz records. I work from home and want to chat a bit when I bring him a tea, without getting in his way.
cases.reply: Tea's here, Marek. I've been enjoying the jazz through the wall all week; my grandad had a stack of jazz records when I was a kid. Who's this playing?
cases.note: Ask about the thing he chose to bring into the room, share one line back, and let him get on with the wall if his answer is short.
